Sorry about the delayed answer. I posted a rather lengthy explanation earlier yesterday, but it somehow did not show here. I will ytry again. Please note that i am just a veteran VTES player and VEKN member, currently in torpor. The reason for asking was that I read a lot about the possibilities of 'publishing a new expansion' and the dispute between the different fractions of the design team. I will not take sides in that discussion, but the whole situation made me wonder about the external representation of the VEKN. It seems that people representing VEKN have been in touch with different companies disussing the options for getting a fan-based expansion into print. As I have recently learned that the VEKN is not a legal entity, I considered how this external representation works. If person A approached company Z, would he or she actually be representing anyone or would that person simply be acting as person A? In the past I assume it did not matter if a person renting a venue for a tournament was a member of VEKN or not, but it seems that 'we' are engaging in business-like activities and might need some sort of legal status. What do you think?

BTW, there is no reason not to trust me. I am just what you perceive I am. Trust me.

Messages.Author: Squidalot

The VEKN will stay separate from any business related activities as it doesn't exist for legal purposes (it's a loose collection of individuals with nominated figureheads) and as the most likely option of POD would be a pickup via DriveThru/related venture they would sort out all the contracts between themselves/wizards/ccp (I would assume), rather than the VEKN.

The VEKN is just a 'pressure group' and organised play group facilitator and more recently rules and design elements have been incorporated. I imagine that the rights to set official cards/rules would go with any POD licence.

I'm suprised that no one has addressed this point that Jeff made.

If VEKN is not a legal entity, then it cannot own anything. Therefore #9 is invalid. Submissions cannot become the legal property of an entity that has no legal standing.

I think the IC members wrote that so that they can use submissions in their new sets without the contributors micromanaging how their submissions are used. That's understandable. They might be better covered by saying "Submissions are considered the property of Johannes Walch (or other VEKN member)". From what I can tell based on the activities of PCK, submissions to VEKN are NOT the property of VEKN.

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
> AaronC wrote:
> If VEKN is not a legal entity, then it cannot own anything. Therefore #9 is invalid. Submissions cannot become the legal property of an entity that has no legal standing.
>
It is not only invalid, it is also inaccurate. If the submission was to be given to VEKN, then at some point the original author would have to stop working on it and hand it over. That's not how it works in practice: people post a first draft, discuss it, amend it, and nobody ever gets to say that the public part is final.

It would be both legally clearer and closer to the intent to replace that point with "Public submissions and amendments of submissions are put in the public domain." It still ensures that the VEKN can use the ideas without hassle, it does not prevent the original author from keeping working on it on his side and it does not require the VEKN to do anything if it rejects the submission.
